```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"

library(ecoTemporalNet)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(readr)
library(knitr)
```

# Overview

This vignette demonstrates how to use `ecoTemporalNet` to build and analyze
temporal overlap networks from frog phenology data.

# Load Data

```{r}
frog1 <- readr::read_csv(
  system.file("extdata", "frogcomtest1.csv", package = "ecoTemporalNet"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

frog2 <- readr::read_csv(
  system.file("extdata", "frogcomtest2.csv", package = "ecoTemporalNet"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

frog3 <- readr::read_csv(
  system.file("extdata", "frogcomtest3.csv", package = "ecoTemporalNet"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

knitr::kable(head(frog1))
```

# Plot Phenology

```{r}
ggplot(frog1, aes(
  x = start_day,
  xend = end_day + 0.5,
  y = reorder(factor(species), -start_day),
  yend = factor(species)
)) +
  geom_segment(linewidth = 8) +
  theme_classic()
```

# Build Network

```{r}
g1 <- create_temporal_network(frog1)
plot(g1,
     vertex.label = igraph::V(g1)$name,
     edge.width = igraph::E(g1)$weight / 5)
```

# Metrics

```{r}
calculate_edge_persistence(frog1)
calculate_latency(g1)
calculate_burstiness(frog1)
calculate_memory_with_latency(frog1)
```
